tldr: Personalization evidence must concern improvement over the best common intervention. In the public two-stratum, three-intervention Bernoulli slice, that causal gain equals \(\max(0,x,y)/(2\sqrt n)\). The exact endpoint \(\zeta_n\) separates a positive-gain region in which every uniformly level-one-tenth test has maximin power one tenth from a region admitting strict improvement. We prove this exact endpoint characterization, explicit legal lower and upper certificates with unmatched exponential bases, and a strict degree-four bracket. Determining \(\zeta_n\) within fixed multiplicative factors through an independently evaluated scale \(b(n)\)—including the exponential base and every unbounded correction—remains the open problem \texttt{oeq:sharp-onset}. Exact likelihood duality and low-degree contacts support that problem; they do not solve its sharp asymptotics.
gap: Sherstov's majority-intersection result gives logarithmic degree, and his optimal-halfspaces result gives sharp linear worst-case degree on Boolean cubes. The compact-domain rational recovery theorem retains multiplicative degree losses, which become different exponential bases after inversion. These results do not determine the continuous square cross-strip endpoint within a bounded multiplicative radius error. The closest archived joint-power proposal also leaves sharp onset coefficients unresolved.
